newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee ambles higher in slow PM trade.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee ambles higher in slow PM trade.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures managed to cling on slight gains by the close on Wednesday in another unimpressive showing.
Traders said values were helped by light trade buying. Otherwise the market could head lower in the absence of fresh supportive news.
Activity picked up a bit in the afternoon on some switch trades with July/Nov spread changing hands at $20.
Overall volume was a tiny 2,823 lots.
The market was called $40-$60 higher but came in just $7 higher on September. The contract finished the day $35 higher at $1,850 per tonne, just $2 off from its session high.
London's dull, range-bound performance mirrored a similar trend in New York arabica futures that had attracted little participation besides the locals.
Traders said the only supportive news was the drawdown in U.S. certified stocks.
"But nothing else is bullish," said one.
Weather in Brazil's coffee areas is also forecast to be mild.
Private U.S. forecaster Weather Services Corp said a warm ridge of high pressure dominating Brazil's coffee belt is expected to continue for the next seven days.
The extended outlook calls for scattered showers in all areas on Saturday and Sunday with temperatures remaining near to above normal. There is no damaging cold expected.
On the charts, analysts said LIFFE's coffee was expected to range sideways.
One analyst described the market as shell-shocked after its recent sharp falls, a factor which militated against a sharp rise.
"If it moves above $2,000 (basis September), it will look a lot better," said Susan Rigg of Chart Analysis. Support is seen at below $1,700, and then down to $1,500.
